analysis: The PR changes only documentation: docs/architecture/inference.md (Flint section, ~lines 2058-2077) and docs/developer/test.md (test names, a new paged-only test description, and the DARKBLOOM_FLINT_BACKEND note). No executable code, protocol, key-handling, attestation, authorization or storage-format source is in the supplied evidence. The doc describes a behavior change: Flint is paged-only. Automatic backend selection is treated as explicit paged, and contiguous selection, the paged kill switch or a capability veto refuses the load instead of falling back. Provider-wide checkpoint defaults (balanced) are ignored for Flint, and non-native explicit selections are refused. I checked this against T-041 (prefix cache, SSD tier, TB-007). The docs describe no change to HMAC lookup tags, TTL, cacheSalt scoping, DBK3 crypto, KEK purge or the DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE kill switch. The test doc says persistent caching is disabled only for fixture isolation. The refusal-instead-of-fallback semantics fail closed and add no attack surface; they carry a minor availability trade-off (a load refused rather than degraded) that the docs state explicitly. The doc claims depend on unsupplied code: EngineV2Factory.prepareProductionBackend, EngineV2KVQuantizationPolicy.resolve and FlintPagedOnlyBackendTests. I could not verify them, and a later pass could confirm the implementation matches the docs, especially that native-only checkpoint precision does not weaken the SSD tier's encrypted-at-rest checkpoint path. No findings are warranted from this documentation-only diff.
